issues.whatGoesWrong: Every wire to the Pi is finished by soldering a cut jumper half (step gpio), and 45 more joints sit in the harness, board and head. Several are hard even for a practised hand (2.0 mm J12 pads, castellated converter pads, XT30 cups, multi-wire 16 AWG nodes).

issues.title: The runtime target guard stops every simulated walk within 0.62 s
issues.whatGoesWrong: Policy targets for hip roll exceed the calibrated +/-0.384 rad; validate_target raises Stop and the runtime torques off all servos mid-step. Measured positions never leave the limits.

evidence.quote: raise Stop('Target exceeds calibrated joint limits: ' + name) ... self.off(str(e))

evidence.number: 33/33 traces trip 0.30 to 0.62 s after the walk command; first offender left hip roll 29, right hip roll 4; 3.3 to 25.5 % of frames out of range; measured qpos never out of range
with clamp 33/33 walk, stop and stay up; speed 0.101 to 0.180 m/s (0.101 to 0.182 without); tilt 4.7 to 9.6 deg (4.8 to 6.8 without)

fix: Clamp walk-mode policy targets to the calibrated limits and log each clamp; keep a hard stop on measured positions outside the limits.
Mirror the clamp in phase1/simulation/evaluate_phase1.py, add a replay test, rebuild the runtime bundle.
Do not rely on XL330 position-limit registers as the main fix.
inferred: hardware will behave like the simulation traces

issues.title: Pi 5 V supply without soldering at the Pi
issues.whatGoesWrong: An all-jumper supply gives 4.58 to 4.69 V at the Pi while walking (rated contacts), below the 4.75 V floor, and adds unlatched male-female junctions in the moving neck loop. The first-power check (4.95 to 5.10 V at pins 2 and 6) fails a correct harness.

evidence.number: run case (0.65 A, motors 7 A, DFR 5.00 V), rated contacts: current guide 4.79 V; 3x20 cm 26 AWG 4.67 V; 3x20 cm 28 AWG 4.60 V; 5x10 cm 28 AWG 4.58 V; 2x30 cm 26 AWG 4.69 V; 22 AWG + lever connector + 10 cm 26 AWG end 4.78 V (4.68 V conservative); doubled 4.80 V

evidence.quote: Measure 4.95–5.10 V at J and at Pi pins 2 and 6.

evidence.number: J 4.95 V at 0.3 A boot load gives 4.886 to 4.914 V at pins 2 to 6

evidence.quote: earlier review specified doubled pins 2+4 / 6+14 with 22 AWG and screened 4.818 V at 1.5 A

fix: Run the existing 22 AWG pair through the notch into the head; inside the cap join each conductor to one cut 26 AWG copper jumper end in a lever connector; pins 2 and 6 only; amplifier stays on pins 4 and 14.

WAGO 221-412 is listed 24 to 12 AWG (0.14 mm2 fine-stranded minimum); 26 AWG is 0.129 mm2. Prefer WAGO 222-412 (28 to 12 AWG, 12.4 x 14.5 x 20.5 mm) if it fits; its fit and the cap-lowering sweep with connectors are unchecked. A 221-412 box fits a pocket near (52.5, 5.5, 138) mm in a 1 mm voxel check.
Use copper jumpers, not CCA.

Replace the first-power line: J 4.95 to 5.10 V unloaded; pins 2 to 6 at least 4.85 V with the Pi idle; at least 4.75 V with camera stream, speaker-test and CPU stress, and J minus pins at most 0.15 V; multimeter only.
verified: Pi, camera, MAX98357A, BNO085 currents from official datasheets
WAGO 221/222 listed ranges and sizes (distributor data)
inferred: Zero W keeps running below 4.75 V

issues.title: The USB-PD receiver is left at its 1.25 A ISET default
issues.whatGoesWrong: With ISET closed the 5991 selects 1.25 A, about 25 W at 20 V or about 4.5 A at 5 V after the converter. Simulated walking peaks at 2.7 to 5.5 A for the servos alone, before the Pi and amplifier. The source may limit or drop the supply mid-walk (inference).

evidence.quote: The ISET jumper must be open for the documented 3.25 A selection.
When the jumper is closed, 1.25A is selected. If the jumper is cut (open), then 3.25A is selected.
pd-tether has no ISET instruction

fix: Add to pd-tether: cut the ISET trace between its pads with a hobby knife and confirm with the meter that the pads no longer beep.
At the loaded bench test confirm source current stays below 3.25 A.
inferred: source enforcement behaviour at the requested current

issues.title: Jaw flex fit: marginal at the guide spread of 5 mm and 2 mm, likely fine when both arms share the spread
issues.verdict: Marginal as written; likely fine with equal thumb force (jaw held loosely so it centres itself).
issues.whatGoesWrong: Step jaw-bench tells the builder to open the -Y arm about 5 mm and the +Y arm about 2 mm. The arm is a thin curved wall (about 1.5 mm thick, 28 to 31 mm2 section between x 41 and 45 mm) printed with horizontal layers, so opening it pulls the layers apart near its thinnest point. At 5 mm the peak layer-normal stress is 15 to 18 MPa against an interlayer adhesion of 17 +/- 3 MPa for Prusament PLA. In-plane strain stays near 1.1 %, well inside the 2.9 % elongation at yield, so the arm is unlikely to whiten before a layer crack (inference).

evidence.quote: Spread the arms with your thumbs as they pass the walls: the −Y arm (with the ring) about 5 mm, the +Y arm about 2 mm.

evidence.number: ear overlap with head_bottom up to 4.739 mm (-Y) and 1.774 mm (+Y) at x 18 to 34 mm; both present together from dz -21.5 to -5.5 mm (total about 6.5 mm); ring and lip pad add nothing; no final-pose overlap

evidence.quote: Moving jaw frame, community-4.stl, PLA, extent [91.41, 69.44, 29.04], "Retained source rotation"; robot-frame extent 68.7 x 91.4 x 29.4 mm, so print Z is robot Z and layers are horizontal

evidence.number: guide 5/2: sigma_zz peak 15.0 MPa, 99.9th percentile 12.3 MPa, principal strain 1.14 %, thumb force 10.3 N (-Y) and 5.6 N (+Y); ear compliance 0.484 / 0.356 mm/N
guide 5/2: sigma_zz peak 17.8 MPa, 99.9th percentile 11.6 MPa, principal 1.07 %
longer free arm (clamp x >= 75): guide 5/2 sigma_zz peak 15.9 MPa, principal 0.95 %

fix: Rewrite the jaw-bench spread instruction: hold the jaw loosely by its front lip so it can slide sideways, and spread both arms at the same time with equal thumb pressure. The jaw centres itself and the arms open about 3.7 mm (-Y) and 2.8 mm (+Y), about 6.5 mm in total, with about 7 to 8 N per thumb.
Change the flex metadata spread [5.0, 2.0] to [3.7, 2.8] so the animation matches.
Keep the stop rule and add: a crack can follow a layer line without white marks, so stop at any click.
Equal-force result: sigma_zz peak 11.3 to 13.3 MPa, 99.9th percentile 7.3 to 9.2 MPa, principal strain 0.71 to 0.86 % across the three models.

issues.title: Runtime current screens may stop the walk; fused groups do not match the guide fuses
issues.whatGoesWrong: The 1.3 A per-servo screen may trip at gait start; GROUPS pairs come from an older fuse layout and do not match the guide's right-leg, left-leg and neck 3 A fuses.

evidence.number: 1.3 A screen trips in 15/33 traces for at least one of five 0.1 s sampling phases, all at t 2.42 to 2.52 s; 5.0 A total trips 1/33 (old120-push, t 5.18 s); 2.25 A pairs 0/33
per-leg RMS at most 1.51 A, worst 1 s mean 1.44 A against 3 A fuses

fix: Log the screens without stopping during the first supported walks, then set limits from measured data with 2 to 3 consecutive samples.
Replace GROUPS with the real fuse branches: IDs 1 to 5, 6 to 10, 11 to 14, each under 3 A.
